item.title: What the Difficult Person on Your Christmas List Really Wants
item.description: We’ve all got one on our Christmas list. The difficult person to shop for, or the person who could have everything. But if I could tell you the truth about so many of us…you might be surprised to know the gift we love the most. We don’t want a gift because it’s expected. Truth is, we’d rather not have a physical gift at all unless it’s something we use regularly or keep on a wishlist for one day. You can give it to us, but there’s a good chance it’ll be donated if we don’t need it or it doesn’t.

item.title: Love, Long after the Vows
item.description: When we pulled into the parking lot of one of our traditional vacation restaurants this year, the lot was unexpectedly empty for a Saturday night. “Uh, oh!” John said. “Looks like this one may be in trouble too.” Our local restaurant with the same name burned over a year ago, and wasn’t rebuilt, and I was looking forward to our yearly vacation visit even more than usual. We walked in, and the restaurant was nearly empty. It took a bit for someone to acknowledge us and lead us to a nearby booth.

item.title: To the Moms Who Love Quiet
item.description: I’ve always been the quiet one. The listener. The observer. The one who never minded silence and didn’t feel the need to fill it. Even as an adult, that part of me never changed. item.title: I Just Want One More Christmas
item.description: I might have missed my son’s last Christmas with Santa. I was there, and I watched it happen, but it never occurred to me that it might be his last. item.title: She May be In Heaven, but I Still Have Coffee with My Mom
item.description: I do not understand how people can get through life without coffee. For me, it is fuel, it gives me energy, and makes me so very happy! Flavored coffee is the best, with lots of milk and sugar. Black coffee? Please, don’t even go there. My mom always loved her coffee too. She would joke that she drank roughly a pot a day, which did not surprise me at all. Mum also loved coffee mugs. item.title: Mom Was the Magic of Christmas
item.description: As I’ve gotten older, I’ve come to realize my mom was the true magic of Christmas. Throughout my childhood, she was the heart and soul of every holiday season, creating an atmosphere filled with warmth, joy, and enchantment. Every December, she transformed our home from top to bottom into a whimsical holiday wonderland.
